summary: All 4 required TDD anchors are present (fire_returnsMonoEmpty, cancelActiveFor_returnsMonoEmpty, fire_acceptsNullPayload, fire_acceptsEmptyPayload). Plain JUnit 5 + Reactor StepVerifier, no Spring context, direct constructor instantiation of NoOpFunnelTriggerService. Style mirrors Task 6's NoOpSubscriberServiceTest exactly (identical imports, field, Duration.ofMillis(100), expectComplete().verify(...) pattern). Litmus test passes: replacing Mono.empty() with Mono.never() would timeout the verify, with Mono.error() would fail expectComplete(), with null would NPE at StepVerifier.create — so the assertions genuinely constrain the implementation rather than tautologically agreeing with it. Tests appropriately scoped — cancelActiveFor takes only non-null args (projectId, chatId) so no null-tolerance case is needed there.

findings.issue: Task description mentions 'returns a non-null Mono'. The current StepVerifier.create(...) form implicitly enforces non-null (passing null throws NPE before any verification runs), so this is covered indirectly but not explicitly named. Not a quality defect — same compromise made in NoOpSubscriberServiceTest — but a one-line assertNotNull on the returned Mono would document the contract explicitly.
findings.recommendation: Optional: capture the result first to make the non-null contract explicit, e.g. `Mono<Void> result = service.fire("proj-A", 200L, "on_start", "ref_smoke_001"); assertNotNull(result); StepVerifier.create(result).expectComplete().verify(Duration.ofMillis(100));`. Skip if Task 6 style consistency is the priority (currently it is, per task `Implementation hints` line: 'Mirror T6 in structure — same patterns, same test style').
